signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Shock
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags a 2.437% weekly spread between leader NOK (+1.526% across 2 pairs) and laggard EUR (-0.910% across 9 pairs), crossing the critical threshold. WTI crude holding above $100.40/bbl reinforces the Norwegian terms-of-trade advantage, while the Norges Bank policy rate of 4.50% carries a +185bp nominal advantage over the ECB deposit facility at 2.65%. Real policy rates amplify this divergence: Norway sits at +1.82% restrictive territory against the Eurozone's +0.34%. In the spot market, EUR/USD trades at 1.1212, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1248), SMA50 (1.1447), and SMA200 (1.1579) in an active downtrend. Technical valuation shows EUR/NOK at 10.4539 trading at a -2.64σ discount to its BEER fair value model, but momentum remains dominant. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/NOK; energy terms-of-trade and policy yield gaps reinforce the bilateral spread. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — market bias hold. Risk: A sharp crude pullback below $95/bbl that compresses the G10 performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Inflation Surge + Options Skew
signals.text: Japan September core CPI accelerated to 2.2% year-on-year against 1.4% expected, while the ex-food and energy print printed at 2.4% against 1.8% consensus. Spot USD/JPY trades at 157.01, maintaining a position below its SMA20 (157.89), SMA50 (157.60), and SMA200 (158.54) following a wide-range bearish daily bar. In the options space, 25-delta risk reversals print an extreme put skew of -2.20 (Saxo Bank, 1M tenor, indicative mid), revealing heavy institutional hedging against USD/JPY downside. OIS SOFR at 3.88% against TONA at 1.23% preserves a +265bp carry buffer in favor of the dollar, but accelerating domestic price pressures raise the probability of a higher BoJ terminal rate. The 160.00 level remains the structural ceiling where verbal warnings historically intensify. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; broadening core inflation pressures and elevated downside options skew outweigh the nominal carry cushion. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — market bias hold. Risk: BoJ policy inertia and dovish guidance that triggers an unwind of downside hedges back above the SMA20 at 157.89.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: Spot USD/NOK trades at 9.3290, printing below its SMA20 (9.512), SMA50 (9.413), and SMA200 (9.518) in an established downtrend extended 2.33 ATR below its 20-day mean. Retail sentiment data retail positioning shows an extreme 100% long reading, contrasting directly with CFTC speculative net flows where non-commercials remain net long the dollar. The Norges Bank policy rate of 4.50% vs Fed 4.00% creates a 50bp rate advantage for the krone, supported by a 2Y sovereign yield gap of -9bp. Spot now trades at -1.69σ below its BEER fair-value model benchmark of 9.4775. The extreme one-sided retail posture presents significant capitulation risk if the broader dollar softening extends into US trade. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; extreme retail long positioning susceptible to cascading stops on trend continuation. Catalyst: US Michigan Consumer Sentiment at 14:00 UTC. Risk: A rebound in broad USD sentiment that reclaims the SMA50 at 9.413 and forces a squeeze on extended spot momentum.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR leveraged funds hold net short -92,833 contracts (CFTC, week ending Oct 13), sitting at the 4th percentile of their 52-week range with a z-score of -1.78. Spot trades at 1.1212, holding beneath its downward-sloping SMA20 (1.1248) and SMA50 (1.1447). Implied volatility runs at 6.8% against HV30 of 4.1%, producing an elevated vol risk premium of +2.7% that reflects sustained institutional demand for tail protection. OIS carry structurally favors the dollar, with SOFR at 3.88% versus €STR at 2.44% providing a +144bp spread, while the 20-day 2Y yield spread moved -29bp in the greenback's favor. However, the extreme crowding of institutional shorts leaves the pair sensitive to short-covering if upcoming US macro prints soften. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry spreads and structural trend remain aligned, though low positioning percentiles restrict aggressive downside chasing. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — market bias hold. Risk: A technical daily close through the SMA20 at 1.1248 triggering speculative short-covering.
